name: two books on one alt market share a rung set under a line row axis (executed-result parity)
description: Seed TWO markets on one 2023 REG week 1 game for one player, both FANDUEL/DRAFTKINGS CLOSE GAME_ALT_PASSING_YARDS OVER, whose ladders overlap but do not coincide -- FanDuel posts 199.5/249.5/299.5, DraftKings posts 249.5/299.5/349.5. This is the line-shopping case the same-quantity rule exists to ADMIT, and it is the feature reason to exist: two books on one market type differing only by source_id. The rung domain is the UNION of both ladders, so the player-week renders FOUR rows, and on a rung only one book posted the other book renders BLANK rather than borrowing its neighbour value or dropping the row. A blank here is real information (that book did not offer that line), which is why the oracle asserts nulls explicitly rather than filtering them out. Both books contribute an OR arm to the player_years_weeks_lines domain; the two books hash to two DISTINCT table aliases because source_id differs, so the columns carry _0 (FanDuel) and _1 (DraftKings) -- unlike the line and odds columns WITHIN one book, which share params, share one alias and so share one suffix. The oracle asserts each row as a four-value tuple rather than four independent columns, because the property under test is that a rung lines up ACROSS books; asserting the columns independently would pass on a query that put FanDuel 199.5 on one row and DraftKings 249.5 on another. Values are derived from the seed.

"prop_market_selections_index" as "pms" on "pms"."source_id" = "m"."source_id" and "pms"."source_market_id" = "m"."source_market_id" and "pms"."time_type" = "m"."time_type" where "player_participation_weeks" as (SELECT pid, year, week, bool_or(is_active) AS is_active
          FROM (SELECT pgl.pid, 2023::int AS year, g.week, pgl.is_active
       FROM player_gamelogs_year_2023 pgl
       INNER JOIN nfl_games g ON g.esbid = pgl.esbid
       WHERE g.season_type = 'REG' AND g.season_year = 2023) src
          GROUP BY pid, year, week), "player_years_teams" as (SELECT pid, year, array_agg(DISTINCT team_code) AS teams

       FROM player_gamelogs_year_2023 pgl
       INNER JOIN nfl_games g ON g.esbid = pgl.esbid
       WHERE g.season_type = 'REG' AND g.season_year = 2023) src
          GROUP BY pid, year), "team_weeks_played" as (select distinct "team", "year", "week" from ((select "home_nfl_team" as "team", "season_year" as "year", "week" from "nfl_games" where "nfl_games"."week" in (1) and "nfl_games"."season_type" in ('REG') and "nfl_games"."season_year" in (2023)) union all (select "away_nfl_team" as "team", "season_year" as "year", "week" from "nfl_games" where "nfl_games"."week" in (1) and "nfl_games"."season_type" in ('REG') and "nfl_games"."season_year" in (2023))) as "g") select "player"."pid", player.first_name, player.last_name, "t95cb9309bbc095bef3ac655cb0ab32bb"."selection_metric_line" AS "game_prop_line_betting_market_0", "t95cb9309bbc095bef3ac655cb0ab32bb"."odds_american" AS "game_prop_american_odds_betting_market_0", "t602ea34e986d44a6ea995577645a9a4e"."selection_metric_line" AS "game_prop_line_betting_market_1", "t602ea34e986d44a6ea995577645a9a4e"."odds_american" AS "game_prop_american_odds_betting_market_1", "player_years_weeks"."year", "player_years_weeks"."week", "player_years_weeks_lines"."selection_metric_line" as "line", CASE
